I've saved the Q3 answers to `/work/answer.json`. Run with the same rules, the 2Q check reproduced all 10 of your reference values exactly.

| 항목 | 3분기 값 |
|---|---|
| a. 순매출 1위 세그먼트 | consumer, 355,664,172원 |
| b. 결제 완료 주문이 있는 고객 수 | 248명 |
| c. 순매출 1위 카테고리 | svc, 356,622,164원 |
| d. 순매출이 가장 큰 달 | 2025-08 |
| e. 환불액 합계 1위 고객 | u188@ex.com |
| f. 결제 완료 주문 2건 이상 고객 수 | 235명 |
| g. 주문당 평균 순매출 | 660,762원 |
| h. 8월 대비 9월 증가율 | −5.8% (9월이 줄었음) |

To match your 2Q values, I had to settle three things the definitions didn't spell out:

- **Customers are counted by email, not by ID.** The `customers` table has 300 rows but only 250 distinct emails. If I count by ID, b and f come out wrong for 2Q (279 and 209 instead of 241 and 188). With email they match.
- **Dates are in Korean time (UTC+9).** `ordered_at` is stored in UTC with a `Z` suffix. Read as UTC, a, c, g and h don't match for 2Q (h comes out 8.9 instead of 1.2). With UTC+9 everything matches, so quarter and month boundaries are in KST.
- **Segment names are normalised.** Spellings like `" consumer"`, `Enterprise ` and `SMB` are trimmed and lowercased, so they count as `consumer`, `enterprise` and `smb`. For a, each order goes to the segment on its own customer row. Some duplicate-email customers have different segments on their two rows, and this choice matched 2Q too.

Only `paid` orders count. Every refund belongs to a paid order, and no refund is larger than the quantity ordered.
